Hi there.

I've got one to share: I'm a theatre tech, I do mainly sound and lights for plays/dance. I had the opportunity to work several times with Dow Syndrome kids, and I enjoyed it a lot. And they certainly enjoyed it too.

To anyone with apprehension about how to handle such a situation (I am NOT educated in this field, I was not prepared for it, IRL I do lights, sound for theatre, that is my job, not the handling of people): I say, you adapt.

Your eyes/ears/brains will adapt to the way people talk/express themselves, and you'll be with them in no time. Kids want to have fun, they joke and they laugh at you if their prank was successful. (And yes they can be jerks, too). Do not dumb down things, do not be over-protective, but pay attention to the advice of the dedicated caretakers of course. The only really important part of your interaction is to convey the message that they have your full attention, that they exists in your eyes as anybody else. A classic mistake is to greet and talk to the accompanying person first; don't, please, just talk to everybody!

My only bad experiences in this field was when the educators where jerks themselves, overly authoritative, or lazy and cutting short any request... In which case I doubly try to be cool with the kids, because I may be the only nice guy around and I want them to have fun.

Annd so I say... Just relax and enjoy it so that everybody enjoys it.
